items.q: An organised association of workers formed to protect their rights and interests is known as a:
opts: Human resources department
Kaizen group
Trade union
Works council
items.why: A trade union is an organised association of workers that collectively bargains for better pay, conditions, and rights. A works council includes management and workers. A trade union is workers only, representing their interests.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: A business that uses a 'chase demand' capacity strategy adjusts its output to match fluctuating demand, often by using flexible contracts or overtime.
Statement 2: A business that operates at full capacity at all times will always maximise its profit.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is correct: chase demand means varying output to follow demand, using flexible staffing and hours. Statement 2 is false: running at full capacity raises unit costs if output cannot be sold, and may damage quality or lead to stockouts; profit depends on revenue and costs together, not capacity utilisation alone.
items.label: New question

items.q: A manager uses decision trees to choose the best financial outcome from four options: A: Expected value = +£2m, Pay-off of best outcome = +£18m B: Net gain = +£3m, Pay-off of best outcome = +£12m C: Net gain = +£2m, Expected value = +£4m D: Net gain = +£1m, Expected value = +£7m Which option is most likely to be chosen?
opts: Option A
Option B
Option C
Option D
items.why: The decision criterion is net gain (expected value minus initial cost). Option B has the highest net gain at +£3m. Option C = +£2m, Option D = +£1m. Option A only shows expected value, not net gain. Net gain = EV - Initial Cost. Always compare net gains.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: A key feature of TQM is the concept of zero defects as a target, aiming to get production right first time.
Statement 2: TQM typically increases short-run costs because it requires investment in training and cultural change, but can reduce long-run costs by cutting waste and rework.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both statements are correct. Zero defects and 'right first time' are central TQM principles. TQM does require significant upfront investment in training and culture change, raising short-run costs, but by preventing defects it reduces waste, rework, and warranty costs over time.
items.label: New question

items.q: In which of these business forms could the owner/owners be required to sell personal assets to pay for business liabilities?
opts: Private limited companies and public limited companies
Private limited companies and sole traders
Public limited companies only
Sole traders only
items.why: Only sole traders have unlimited liability, meaning personal assets can be seized to pay business debts. Both private and public limited companies have limited liability - shareholders can only lose the amount they invested. 'Limited' in the name means limited liability.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Lower UK interest rates are likely to lead to an increase in UK exports because they probably lead to:
opts: A rise in costs of UK businesses and a rise in the exchange rate of the pound
A rise in costs of UK businesses and a fall in the exchange rate of the pound
A fall in costs of UK businesses and a rise in the exchange rate of the pound
A fall in costs of UK businesses and a fall in the exchange rate of the pound
items.why: Lower rates reduce borrowing costs (fall in costs) and cause the pound to depreciate as foreign investors seek better returns elsewhere (fall in exchange rate). A weaker pound makes UK exports cheaper abroad. The mechanism: lower rates -> less foreign investment -> less demand for pounds -> pound falls -> exports cheaper.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Parkside Engineering introduces total quality management (TQM). Which of the following best describes what this requires from the workforce?
opts: A dedicated quality control department inspects all output before dispatch.
Every employee takes responsibility for quality in their own area of work.
Quality targets are set centrally and monitored by senior management only.
Automated machinery replaces human involvement in the production process.
items.why: TQM is a whole-organisation approach in which every employee is responsible for quality at every stage — it is not confined to a specialist department or senior management. Students often confuse TQM with quality control, which uses a dedicated inspection team.
items.label: New question

items.q: Budgeted income £200m, budgeted expenditure £160m. Actual income as budgeted but expenditure 20% higher. The actual profit showed:
opts: A favourable variance of £8m
A favourable variance of £32m
An adverse variance of £8m
An adverse variance of £32m
items.why: Budgeted profit = 200 - 160 = £40m. Actual expenditure = 160 x 1.2 = £192m. Actual profit = 200 - 192 = £8m. Variance = 8 - 40 = -£32m. This is an adverse variance (actual profit lower than budgeted). 20% of £160m = £32m extra expenditure. This directly reduces profit by £32m.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Collective bargaining means that a trade union negotiates pay and conditions on behalf of its members as a group, giving workers greater bargaining power than individuals acting alone.

Statement 2: A closed shop arrangement means workers are free to choose whether to join a trade union at a particular workplace.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 is true: collective bargaining pools the negotiating power of all union members, making it harder for employers to impose terms on individuals. Statement 2 is false: a closed shop is an arrangement (now unlawful in the UK) where all employees must belong to a specified trade union — the opposite of free choice.
items.label: New question

items.q: A good has negative YED and negative PED. Statement 1: 'A fall in incomes must lead to a fall in sales volume.' Statement 2: 'A fall in price must lead to a rise in sales value.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both false. Statement 1: negative YED = inferior good, so income fall causes demand to rise. Negative YED = inferior good = demand increases when income falls. 'Must' is too strong for Statement 2.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Lynton Foods uses quality control rather than quality assurance. Which of the following is most likely to be a disadvantage of this approach compared with quality assurance?
opts: It requires every employee to take individual responsibility for checking quality standards at every stage of production, increasing training costs.
Defective products may only be identified after resources have already been used to make them.
It makes it harder to set measurable quality standards because inspection criteria must be agreed across all departments rather than by specialists alone.
It removes the need for a specialist quality inspection team, increasing labour costs.
items.why: Quality control checks happen at the end of production, so waste and defective materials have already been used up before problems are spotted. Quality assurance catches errors earlier in the process, reducing waste. Option A describes a feature of QA, not QC.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Quality control involves checking products at the end of the production process, whereas quality assurance involves building quality checks into every stage of production.
Statement 2: Quality assurance eliminates the need for any inspection of finished goods.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 correctly distinguishes the two approaches: quality control is an end-of-process check, while quality assurance embeds checks throughout. Statement 2 is false because assurance reduces but does not necessarily eliminate the need for final inspection — some firms still check finished output even with QA systems in place.
items.label: New question

items.q: Which is MOST likely the result of successful employee engagement?
opts: Higher labour costs per unit
Higher trade union membership
Lower labour productivity
Lower labour turnover
items.why: Engaged employees are more committed and satisfied, so they're less likely to leave - resulting in lower labour turnover. A, B, and C are negative outcomes that engagement should reduce, not cause. Employee engagement = commitment and motivation. The most direct measurable benefit is reduced staff turnover.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Statement 1: 'The path with the lowest total float time is the critical path.' Statement 2: 'At least one activity must have a float time.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 true: the critical path has zero float (the lowest possible). All other paths have some float. Statement 2 false: it's possible for all activities to be on the critical path (if there's only one path through the network), meaning no activity has float. In a simple linear network (A->B->C), every activity is critical and none has float. So Statement 2 is false.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: Creston Hotels faces highly seasonal demand, with occupancy rates of 95% in summer and 40% in winter. Which strategy would best help the business match supply to demand throughout the year?
opts: Build additional hotels to increase maximum capacity during peak summer periods, ensuring no customers are turned away.
Use dynamic pricing and flexible staffing levels to manage demand and costs across seasons.
Maintain a constant workforce and identical room rates throughout the year to simplify administration and ensure consistent staffing budgets.
Switch to a just-in-time inventory system to reduce storage costs for consumables such as toiletries and linen across both seasons.
items.why: Dynamic pricing can stimulate demand in low seasons and manage excess demand in peak periods, while flexible staffing reduces labour costs when occupancy is low. Building more capacity would worsen the winter underutilisation problem, and JIT relates to inventory, not capacity management in a hotel context.
items.label: New question

items.q: Statement 1: 'In SWOT, high staff turnover is a threat.' Statement 2: 'In SWOT, excellent R&D facilities are an opportunity.'
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both false. High staff turnover is a weakness (internal factor), not a threat (external). Excellent R&D facilities are a strength (internal asset), not an opportunity (external). SWOT: Strengths and Weaknesses are internal. Opportunities and Threats are external.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q:
Statement 1: Crowdfunding via an equity platform and a traditional share issue both involve selling ownership stakes in the business in return for finance.

Statement 2: A business that raises finance through a share issue is obliged to repay the capital to shareholders at the end of an agreed term.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Both equity crowdfunding and a conventional share issue give investors a share of ownership, so Statement 1 is true. Share capital is permanent finance — unlike a loan, it does not have to be repaid on a fixed date, so Statement 2 is false. This is a key distinction between equity and debt finance.
items.label: New question

items.q: A business moves an employee to a different job. This is known as:
opts: Delayering
Delegating
Redeployment
Redundancy
items.why: Redeployment means moving an existing employee to a different role within the organisation. Redeployment = the employee moves to a different job.
items.label: Past paper question

items.q: On an inventory control chart, what does the 'buffer inventory' level represent?
opts: The quantity of stock ordered each time a new order is placed, calculated by dividing annual demand by the number of orders placed per year.
The minimum level of stock held to protect against unexpected increases in demand or delivery delays.
The stock level at which a new order is automatically triggered, calculated by multiplying average daily usage by the supplier's lead time in days.
The maximum quantity of stock that the business's warehouse can physically hold before additional storage facilities would be required.
items.why: Buffer (or safety) stock is held as a precaution against stockouts caused by demand spikes or late deliveries. The reorder level (option C) is the trigger point for placing a new order, which is a different concept students frequently confuse with buffer stock.
items.label: New question

items.q:
Statement 1: Holding a large buffer inventory reduces the risk of stockouts but increases stockholding costs such as storage, insurance, and opportunity cost of capital.
Statement 2: Just-in-time (JIT) production relies on holding a large buffer inventory to ensure production never stops.
opts: Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is true. Statement 2 is false.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is true.
Statement 1 is false. Statement 2 is false.
items.why: Statement 1 correctly identifies the trade-off: more buffer stock lowers stockout risk but raises holding costs. Statement 2 is false: JIT is specifically designed to minimise or eliminate buffer inventory by receiving stock only when it is needed for production, relying instead on reliable supplier relationships.
items.label: New question
